messages:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing increased volume for tracing across several tenants. I want to propose a per-customer dynamic span TTL + export-filtering layer so high-volume tenants get aggressive retention and sampled exports while critical traces still make it to long-term stores. Proposal sketch: compute TTL from QPS + error-rate, add export_policy tags for downstream adapters. Thoughts?

oliver: Agree in principle. Can we compute TTL based on a sliding window of recent QPS + error-rate? Also need a way to pin specific trace ids (or service rollouts) so we don't lose important traces during deployment incidents.

sam: Quick question — how do we apply this consistently across Tempo/Jaeger/Honeycomb/Datadog/Splunk? My idea: central muxer that annotates spans with an `export_policy` header and exporter adapters drop/route based on a per-customer config. That keeps backend-specific logic isolated.

dina: :+1: but watch out for vendor constraints — Tempo prefers full traces for debug, Honeycomb customers expect high-cardinality fields preserved, and Datadog has strict ingest size limits. We'll need adapter-level transforms instead of global truncation.

leo: Suggest a two-tier policy: 1) short-lived prefix/KV cache retention for hot traces, 2) raw export sampling with an anomaly reservoir that picks some full traces for long-term storage. Reservoir selection can be trace_id-hash based with a fast path for error spans.

oliver: Sketch of config (per-customer YAML):
```yaml
export_policy:
  dynamic_ttl: true
  ttl_seconds: 86400 # baseline, scaled by load
  max_sample_rate: 0.01
  anomaly_reservoir_size: 2000
  backend_priorities: [tempo, honeycomb, datadog]
  fallback_export: longterm-s3
```

sam: Implementation notes: exporter adapters must emit drop metrics with `drop_reason` labels and expose counters for sampled vs full traces. Also we should add a `fallback_export` option that writes compressed traces to cheap object storage instead of dropping.

travis: For Splunk/Datadog especially, ingest cost matters — maybe we synthesize low-cardinality aggregates (service-level latency histograms) for heavy tenants instead of full spans, and preserve a small reservoir of full traces for anomalies.

maya: Action items: oliver to prototype muxer and config schema, sam to wire adapter metrics and fallback export, dina to audit backend constraints and document per-vendor caveats, leo to design reservoir algorithm and simulation. Can we meet Friday to review prototype and UX for the console retention controls? Also: add a flag to pin traces during canary rollouts.

oliver: On it. I'll spin up a minimal muxer PR and post a design doc with config schema.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of trace-muxer started in prod-us-01 (build 0.3.2) :rocket:

maya: Thanks all. Leave any vendor-specific gotchas here — particularly if Honeycomb/Tempo/Datadog adapters need extra fields or we risk exceeding their ingestion contracts.
